summary: N. J. Francis is an indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed a master's degree in ancient history at the University of Calicut and conducted doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya (1928–2017) was an indologist and philosopher. He served as Vice Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and was a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1989–2017).

N. Veezhinathan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under T. M. P. Mahadevan, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and doctoral supervisor A. Sankaran, earning a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964. He was a research scholar at Deccan College (1960–1963) and became Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras and as Deputy Director for Epigraphy at the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh.

Nae Ionescu (1890–1940) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Bucharest (~1908–1912), University of Göttingen (~1913–1914), and University of Munich (~1916–1919), and held a post at the University of Bucharest (~1920–1938).
Nagin J. Shah is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Succeeding Dalsukh Malvania, he served as Acting Director of the L. D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Chittagong College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta (PhD ~1918–1921), and SOAS/University of London (DLitt ~1923–1925) under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served at Judson College (~1917–1920), University of Calcutta (~1924–1958), The Asiatic Society (1959–1961), and Maha Bodhi Society (1959–1973).

Nalini Balbir is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Colette Caillat (~1977–1986). She held posts at CNRS (1982–1988), INALCO (~1988–2000), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (from 1988), EPHE (from 2000), and the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Nalini Devdas is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She studied under Paul David Devanandan, C. T. Krishnamachari, Steven Collins, Richard P. Hayes, and supervisor Leslie C. Orr, earning a PhD from Concordia University (attested 2004), and held a post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history-archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Helen Hardacre, Fumio Tamamuro, and Martin Collcutt, followed by a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard and a professorship at the University of British Columbia (attested 2000).

Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and serves as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche (1931–2003) was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary, University of Michigan, and under traditional teachers Sayadaw U Thila Wunta, Mahasi Sayadaw, Chao Khun Phra Rajasiddhimuni, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

Namio Egami (1906–2002) was a historian, archaeologist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), where he later held a post (~1948–1967), and served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Derge Gonchen, Khams-bre Shedra, and Kuse Serjong Shedra under various traditional teachers. He held posts at Southwest Minzu University, IsMEO, and the University of Naples (1962–1992), and founded the Shang Shung Institute in 1990.

Nancy E. Levine is an anthropologist working in Tibetology and related fields. She has served on the anthropology faculty at the University of California, Los Angeles, as Associate Professor (attested 1998) and Professor (attested 2026).

Nancy G. Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley (PhD), and holds an endowed professorship in Buddhist chaplaincy and Tibetan and South Asian studies at the Numata Center (attested 2026).

Nancy Hock is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1987), where she was supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams, and held a post at the Asian Art Museum (attested 1987).

Nancy McCagney is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson. She held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nancy S. Steinhardt is a historian, archaeologist, and sinologist. Since ~1982, she has served at the University of Pennsylvania as Professor of East Asian Art and Curator of Chinese Art at the Penn Museum.
